342793.title: Shahriari and Yu's conjecture for forbidden copies of $Y_k$ and $Y'_k$
342793.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $\mathrm{La}_q(n,\{Y_k,Y'_k\})$ denote the maximum size of a family of subspaces of an $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ containing neither $Y_k$ nor $Y'_k$ as a subposet. Let $\Sigma_q(n,k)$ denote the corresponding sum of the $k$ largest Gaussian binomial coefficients. **Shahriari and Yu's conjecture.** For $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq k+1$, 

$$
\mathrm{La}_q(n,\{Y_k,Y'_k\})=\Sigma_q(n,k).
$$

The conjecture is a vector-space analogue of a forbidden-poset theorem in the Boolean lattice; the cited paper proves this result using the $q$-analogue of the Lubell–Yamamoto–Meshalkin inequality.

342841.title: Dorbec et al.'s power domination bound for connected regular graphs
342841.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $r$-regular graph of order $n$, with $r\ge 3$, and let $k\ge 1$. Write $\gamma_{p,k}(G)$ for the minimum cardinality of a $k$-power dominating set of $G$. Assume that $G\not\cong K_{r,r}$. **Dorbec et al.'s conjecture.** Then

$$
\gamma_{p,k}(G)\le \frac{n}{r+1}.
$$

This conjecture extends known upper bounds for $k$-power domination in regular graphs by removing the claw-free hypothesis. Its status is unclear from the supplied text.

342842.title: Claw-free regular graph power domination conjecture

$$
\gamma_{p,k}(G)\le \frac{n}{k+l+2},

342846.title: Existence of a dfs measure that is not finitely approximated
342846.literal_statement:

342868.title: Il'yuta's monotone-cycle conjecture for Coxeter–Dynkin diagrams
342868.literal_statement: Assume $n\equiv2\pmod 4$. Let $D$ be a Coxeter–Dynkin diagram, with vertices given by a distinguished basis and edge weights $\langle\delta_i,\delta_j\rangle$. A **monotone cycle** is a sequence of vertices $(\delta_{i_1},\ldots,\delta_{i_k})$ with $i_1<\cdots<i_k$, in which each $\delta_{i_j}$ is connected to $\delta_{i_{j+1}}$, with indices taken cyclically. Let ${\mathcal D}$ denote the collection of such diagrams, and let the modality be the modality of the singularity. **Il'yuta's monotone-cycle conjecture.** The minimum over all $D\in{\mathcal D}$ of the smallest number of edges that must be deleted so that $D$ contains no monotone cycles is equal to the modality of the singularity. The conjecture was disproved by counterexamples for bimodal singularities.

342985.title: The edge-addition conjecture for rooted phylogenetic networks
342985.literal_statement:
Let $N$ be a rooted phylogenetic network on leaf set $X$. The quantities $\ell(N)$ and $e(N)$ measure, respectively, the tree-based proximity of $N$ and the minimum number of directed edges that must be added to make $N$ tree-based. **Edge-addition conjecture.** There exists a set of directed edges that can be added to $N$ to turn it into a tree-based rooted phylogenetic network on leaf set $X$. Furthermore,

$$
\ell(N)\le e(N)\le 2\ell(N).
$$

The conjecture asserts both that every rooted phylogenetic network can be made tree-based by adding directed edges and that the required number of additions is at most twice its tree-based proximity. The preceding example shows that the unrooted equality $e(N)=\ell(N)$ does not extend to rooted networks, since there $e(N)=2>1=\ell(N)$.

342989.title: Gupta's co-density conjecture for multigraph cover index
342989.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph. Its cover index $\xi(G)$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint edge covers of $G$, and its minimum degree is $\delta(G)$. Define the co-density by

$$
\Phi(G)=\min\left\\{\frac{2|E^+(U)|}{|U|+1}: U\subseteq V,\ |U|\geq 3\text{ and odd}\right\\},
$$

where $E^+(U)$ consists of the edges with at least one end in $U$. **Gupta's co-density conjecture.** Every multigraph $G$ satisfies

$$
\xi(G)\geq \min\\{\delta(G)-1,\\,\lfloor \Phi(G) \rfloor\\}.
$$

The conjecture is the cover-packing counterpart of the Goldberg–Seymour edge-coloring conjecture. Its validity would constrain the cover index to two possible values relative to the fractional cover index; the paper reports only approximate bounds as known.

342990.title: Gupta's characterization conjecture for the cover-index lower bound
342990.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$ and maximum edge multiplicity $\mu(G)$. Suppose that $\delta(G)$ cannot be expressed in the form

$$
2p\mu(G)-q
$$

for any integers $p$ and $q$ satisfying $q\geq 0$ and $p>\mu(G)+\left\lfloor (q-1)/2\right\rfloor$. **Gupta's characterization conjecture.** Then

$$
\xi(G)\geq \delta(G)-\mu(G)+1.
$$

Gupta proposed this as a complete characterization of the parameter values for which equality in the general lower bound $\xi(G)\geq \delta(G)-\mu(G)$ cannot occur. The paper presents the statement as a conjecture and does not report a resolution.

343041.title: Generalized Nagao conjecture for hyperelliptic Jacobians
343041.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a hyperelliptic curve defined over $\mathbb{Q}(T)$ whose Jacobian $J_{\mathcal{X}}$ has no subvariety defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. For an integer $t$, let $a_{\mathcal{X}_t}(p)=p+1-\#\mathcal{X}_t(\mathbb{F}_p)$ and define

$$
A_{\mathcal{X},1}(p)=\frac{1}{p}\sum_{t=0}^{p-1}a_{\mathcal{X}_t}(p).
$$

**Generalized Nagao conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{P \to \infty} \frac{1}{P} \sum_{p \leq P} -A_{\mathcal{X},1}(p) \log p=\operatorname{rank} J_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathbb{Q}(T)).
$$

The conjecture is proposed as the rank-detecting generalization of Nagao's conjecture for hyperelliptic Jacobians. The paper uses it conditionally to construct high-rank examples, and no resolution status is supplied here.

343173.title: Aldous–Fill spectral-gap conjecture for regular graphs
343173.literal_statement:

$$
(1+o(1))\frac{2k\pi^2}{3n^2},

This is an equivalent spectral-gap formulation of the conjecture on maximum relaxation time. The paper proves it for cubic graphs, while the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.

343183.title: Beck–Fiala conjecture for regular hypergraphs
343183.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a $t$-regular hypergraph, meaning that every vertex belongs to exactly $t$ hyperedges. For a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}=(V,E)$, let $\operatorname{disc}(\mathcal{H})$ denote its discrepancy, the minimum over all $\pm1$ colorings of the maximum absolute signed edge sum.

**Beck–Fiala conjecture.** For a $t$-regular hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$, we have

$$
\operatorname{disc}(\mathcal{H})=O(\sqrt{t}).
$$

This is one of the central open problems in discrepancy theory; the paper’s main spectral bound gives an $O(\sqrt{t}+\lambda)$ estimate, but does not establish the conjectured bound for general $t$-regular hypergraphs.

343185.literal_statement:

343191.title: Non-smash-product conjecture for the generalized symmetry bialgebroid
343191.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be the finite set underlying the function algebra $C(X)$, and let $H$ be the smallest subalgebra of $C(X \times X \times X \times X)$ containing $C(X)$ and the set $H_0$ of functions satisfying the three displayed conditions in the construction above. The resulting $H$ is a left bialgebroid over $C(X)$ whose action on $C(X)$ lifts to universal one forms. **Non-smash-product conjecture.** $H$ is not of the form

$$
C(X)\# Q
$$

for any Hopf algebra $Q$ acting on $C(X)$. This asserts that the generalized symmetry bialgebroid constructed here cannot in general be represented as a smash product by an acting Hopf algebra.

343193.title: Brown–Erdős–Sós and Alon–Shapira conjecture on sparse hypergraph exponents
343193.literal_statement:
Let $f_r(n,v,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $r$-graph on $n$ vertices such that every set of $v$ vertices spans at most $e-1$ edges. For fixed integers $r>k\ge 2$ and $e\ge 3$, consider $f_r(n,er-(e-1)k+1,e)$. **Brown–Erdős–Sós and Alon–Shapira conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$,

$$
n^{k-o(1)}<f_r(n,er-(e-1)k+1,e)=o(n^k).
$$

The upper bound is known in the stated parameter range, and several lower-bound cases are known; the smallest unresolved case is whether $f_3(n,7,4)=o(n^2)$.
343193.source_name: Chong Shangguan and Itzhak Tamo, “Degenerate Turán densities of sparse hypergraphs”, arXiv:1907.04930 (2020).

343219.title: Caro–Hegarty–Morrison quadratic-order conjecture for arithmetic-progression zero sums
343219.literal_statement:
Let $r$ and $s$ be fixed positive integers. For a function $f:[n]\to\{-r,s\}$ with $f([n])=0$, let $M(r,s,k)$ denote the minimum threshold such that every sufficiently large $n$ forces a zero-sum $k$-term arithmetic progression. **Caro–Hegarty–Morrison's conjecture.** There are positive constants $c_1=c_1(r,s)$ and $c_2=c_2(r,s)$ such that

$$
c_1k^2\le M(r,s,k)\le c_2k^2.
$$

Thus the threshold for zero-sum arithmetic progressions has quadratic order in $k$. Existing results give superlinear lower bounds and quadratic upper bounds, but the matching quadratic lower bound remains open.

343269.title: Outerplanar graph polygon-chain determination conjecture
343269.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bi-connected outerplanar graph. Let $G^*$ be its inner dual, and let $P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_t$ be the polygon chain decomposition of $G$ corresponding to the maximal path decomposition of $G^*$. Write $\tau(P_i)$ for the number of spanning trees of $P_i$, and let $\mu(G)$ denote the minimum number of generators of the sandpile group $S(G)$. **Polygon-chain determination conjecture.** The quantity $\mu(G)$ is determined by the numbers

$$
\tau(P_1),\ldots,\tau(P_t).
$$

For polygon flowers, the analogous assertion follows from the paper's results; the conjecture extends this phenomenon to all bi-connected outerplanar graphs, and its resolution is not given in the source.

343283.title: Recursive muffin-algorithm value conjecture
343283.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a 3M-DAP that is not a 0-problem, and let $P'$ be the smaller 3M-DAP obtained from $P$ by one application of the recursive algorithm. Let $g(P)$ denote the size of the smallest piece in the solution produced by that algorithm.

**Recursive value conjecture.** For any 3M-DAP $P$ that is not a 0-problem,

$$
g(P)=g(P').
$$

The source says that it proves this conjecture in the subsequent analysis. Therefore its status is solved.

343327.title: Malle–Robinson conjecture on simple modules in blocks of finite groups
343327.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a finite group. For subgroups $N\unlhd K\subseteq H$, call $K/N$ a **section** of $H$. Define the **sectional $\ell$-rank** $s(H)$ to be the maximum rank of an elementary abelian $\ell$-section of $H$. For a block $B$ of $H$, let $l(B)$ denote the number of irreducible Brauer characters in $B$. If $B$ is an $\ell$-block of $H$ with defect group $D$, then

**Malle–Robinson conjecture.**

$$
l(B)\leq \ell^{s(D)}.
$$

This conjecture bounds the number of simple modules in a block by the sectional $\ell$-rank of its defect group. The supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.

343332.title: Minimum-weight MIPPR word conjecture for minimal PPRIC codes
343332.literal_statement: Let $r$, $s$, and $L$ be nonnegative integers with $L\geqslant 2s+r+1$, and let $C\subseteq {\cal W}_s$ be a minimal $(L,s,r)$ PPRIC code. 343345.title: Berger–Wang conjecture for modified EGZ constants in powers of $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})$
343345.literal_statement:
For positive integers $n=2^k$ and $d\geq 1$, let $s'_n(G)$ denote the modified Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant of a finite abelian group $G$. Let $\ell$ be the smallest integer such that $\ell\geq 2^d$ and $\ell\nmid n$. **Berger–Wang conjecture.** One has

$$
s'_n\left((\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^d\right)=2^d n-\ell+1.
$$

The conjecture is presented as an open problem concerning modified EGZ constants in higher-dimensional groups; no resolution is given in the source.

343369.title: Jiang–Polyanskii conjecture for infinite spectral radius order
343369.literal_statement:
Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$, let $N_\alpha(d)$ be the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common angle parameter $\alpha$, and set

$$
\lambda=\frac{1-\alpha}{2\alpha}.
$$

For a real $\lambda>0$, let $k(\lambda)$ be the smallest number of vertices of a graph whose spectral radius is exactly $\lambda$, with $k(\lambda)=\infty$ if no such graph exists.

**Jiang–Polyanskii conjecture.** If $k(\lambda)=\infty$, then

$$
N_\alpha(d)=d+O_\alpha(1).
$$

The paper explains that its main theorem gives only $N_\alpha(d)=d+O_\alpha(d/\log\log d)$ in this case, while the conjectured bounded excess over $d$ remains open. It also notes that the conjecture had been verified except when $\lambda$ is a totally real algebraic integer that is largest among its conjugates.

343382.title: Independent-set bound for graphs excluding a clique minor
343382.literal_statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote the size of its largest independent set. **Independent-set bound for clique-minor-free graphs.** If $G$ does not contain $K_{t+1}$ as a minor, then

$$
\alpha(G)\geq \frac{n}{t}.
$$

This bound would follow from Hadwiger's conjecture, since every $n$-vertex graph has chromatic number at least $\lceil n/\alpha(G)\rceil$. Duchet and Meyniel proved the bound within a factor of $2$, and subsequent work improved the factor; the exact bound remains open in general.

343428.title: Extremal number conjecture for matching blow-ups of complete bipartite graphs
343428.literal_statement:
Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $s\leq t$, let $p\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal{M}(K^{p+1}_{s,t})$ denote the matching blow-up family used in the paper. Let $h(n,1,s)$ and $f(t-1,t-1)$ be the functions defined in the paper. **Matching blow-up extremal-number conjecture.** If $n\geq s+2t$ and $p\geq 3$, then

$$
\emph{ex}(n,\mathcal{M}(K^{p+1}_{s,t}))=h(n,1,s)+f(t-1,t-1)-\left\lceil\frac{s-1}{2}\right\rceil+i,
$$

where $i=1$ if $s=t$ is even and $i=0$ otherwise. The conjecture concerns the exact extremal number for the matching blow-up of $K_{s,t}$, which the paper does not determine in its theorem; its resolution is not supplied here.
343428.source_name: Long-Tu Yuan, “Extremal graphs for edge blow-up of graphs”, arXiv:1908.02025 (2021).

343429.title: Revised conjecture for the non-monochromatic extremal function
343429.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a given graph, and let $g(n,G)$ denote the maximum number of edges not contained in any monochromatic copy of $G$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of $K_n$. Let $\emph{ex}(n,G)$ denote the extremal number of $G$. **Revised non-monochromatic extremal conjecture.** If $n$ is sufficiently large, then there exists a constant $h_G$ depending on $G$ such that

$$
g(n,G)=\emph{ex}(n,G)+h_G.
$$

This revises the earlier equality conjecture after the paper exhibits counterexamples to it. The asserted bounded additive correction is left open in the supplied text.

343452.title: Maximum-row-degree exponent conjecture for zero-one matrices
343452.literal_statement:
Let $t\geq 2$ be a positive integer, and let $A$ be a zero-one matrix such that every row of $A$ contains at most $t$ $1$-entries. **Maximum-row-degree exponent conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,A)=n^{2-\frac{1}{t}+o(1)}.
$$

This is presented as a strengthening of results proved in the paper and remains open. The authors note that even the case of matrices corresponding to cycles is of interest.

343454.title: Heil's minimum-volume conjecture for bodies of given thickness
343454.literal_statement: Let $d$ be a prescribed thickness, and consider convex bodies in three-dimensional space with thickness $d$. The **Heil body** is the convex hull of six circular arcs of radius $d$, centered at the midpoints of the edges of a regular tetrahedron of edge length $d\sqrt{2}$, together with the four vertices of a rescaled tetrahedron of edge length $d(2\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})/3$. **Heil's conjecture.** The Heil body is the minimum-volume three-dimensional body in the class of convex bodies with given thickness. The conjecture concerns the unresolved minimum-volume problem for convex bodies of prescribed thickness; the source gives no resolution.
